description:
After a clean merge a dependent can stay `backlog` with nothing unmet and nothing reporting it, so it never becomes available until someone runs `jit validate --fix`.

## Background

Found while testing `aeafc378` on a scratch clone. Two linked checkouts each close one of a dependent's two blockers. Each checkout sees one blocker still open, so neither promotes the dependent. The branches merge with no conflict, and on the merged state the dependent is `backlog`, has no unmet dependencies, and is absent from `jit query available`. The worker reported `jit validate` passing on that state, and `jit validate --fix` repairing it.

945f9181 (one readiness derivation) adds the pure correction function and carries it into deletion, dependency edits and template edges. It does not cover a state produced by a merge or what validation reports, so this bug links to it rather than duplicating it.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `jit validate` on a repository whose stored readiness disagrees with the dependency graph reports each such issue and fails, rather than passing silently.
- [hard] REQ-02: `jit validate --fix` still repairs it, and `jit validate` then passes.
- [hard] REQ-03: A test reproduces the two-blocker merged state and owns REQ-01 and REQ-02.
- [hard] REQ-04: The readiness comparison uses `Issue::derive_readiness_correction`, with no second derivation.

## Notes

- Reproduce on the merged state first and record the result here before changing code.
- Related: 945f9181.
title: Validation reports a promotion the graph demands
